a.text: 'Not every meeting has a beautiful ending, Amiya.'
'A lot of stories end suddenly. A lot of stories keep us tossing and turning in our beds. And some stories end... with a long, long sigh.'
'In a wilderness without end, people meet and go their separate ways. But at the crucial moment when we cross paths...'
'No one knows if we should really be saying such solemn goodbyes.'

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Come in.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Theresa, you're back!

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Amiya?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: What's the matter? Look what time it is. You should be in bed, if you don't want Kal'tsit getting angry with you.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I know, but... I can't sleep.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Want me to sleep with you?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I-It's okay! If you still have work to do, I—

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: You've been waiting for me all day, haven't you? Did something happen?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Nope! I... Everyone's been very nice to me, and I'm keeping up with my homework, too. I've finished all the assignments Dr. Kal'tsit gave me!

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I know you've been really busy and I shouldn't bother you, but... I don't know why... I really wanted to see you today.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Is that right?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Come, Amiya. I'm here.
Theresa kneels down and hugs Amiya.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I'm here for you now.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Alright.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I... I saw you standing here, waiting by yourself while everybody else was gone for so, so long... I still remember the look on your face. I don't get it...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Are you worried about something? Isn't everyone saying we're about to win?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Yes, there's always good news.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Our fighters captured another town. We advanced our position once more... Kazdel, our home, is closer than ever.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Amiya, Babel still has a very long journey ahead of us. Our goal is so far away... I don't actually even know if we're still sailing toward our original destination.
Theresa lets out a brief sigh and looks into the distance. Amiya follows Theresa's gaze, but finds nothing.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Babel does not exist to win victories. It never has.

spans.text: Babel does not exist to win

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Victories and scars go hand-in-hand, and... those scars are far more difficult than we ever anticipated to heal.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Or rather... Can they even be healed?
Theresa's voice is very soft, almost like a dream melted away in water. As a cloud of mist rises, the brief, momentary smile that she had before now seems distant and hazy.
The young Cautus girl thinks that, for a moment or two, the woman holding her hand all this time almost seemed to have disappeared into the mist herself.

And so Amiya makes the effort to stand on her tiptoes and stretches her hand out. The young girl's soft fingertips touch the forehead between the eyes of the King of Sarkaz; she tries to smooth those knitted brows.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: They can... They will.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Theresa, I still remember what you told me.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: 'Perhaps, one day... We'll be able to let everyone on this vast land fall into peaceful slumber.'

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Right. That includes you... and me.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Go, Amiya. We have lots of time to talk about the future, but if you stay up all night, you won't be getting any taller.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: What are you going to do if you're still a teeny tiny bean by the time Rhodes Island is proudly sailing across the vast lands?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: *whimper*...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: If I... If I point my ears up, I'll look taller, won't I?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Pff... Haha...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: You really don't want to go back to your room, don't you?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I-I'm not being naughty! I'm just—

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Alright, let's not tell Kal'tsit, then. You can stay a little longer.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: It's been a while since I told you a story, hasn't it?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: It's okay. I still remember all the stories you told me!

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: 'A long time ago, there was a great, big desert and a tiny, little doll made of sackcloth. The little puppet swore he would cross the desert to find the legendary Plains of Hope...'

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: But you've never told me how the story ends—

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Oh, that one, huh...?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: There were a lot of scary things out there in the desert. If I were to tell you, you'd never sleep again.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I'm not scared of them. Besides, with you telling the story, I'm sure it'll have a nice ending.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Alright.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: The desert...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: It was so vast and wide, like there was no end to it.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Our little puppet had been through many great adventures, and at last, he made it. His goal was right in front of him. The Plains of Hope...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: What were the plains like?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Hm... The kind of place that anyone would like to call home.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: The kind of place with all the carrot pies I could eat? With everybody on the landship there, too?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Maybe.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: But things are never that easy in these stories. He still had to overcome the last obstacle that stood in his way.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: The desert was very cold, and the wind there never stopped. In the light of the twin moons, there seemed to be some black cloaked shadows whispering to themselves, but the moment he looked for them, they disappeared.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: What were the black cloaked shadows?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: They were the echoes of the oldest despair and sadness. If they catch you, you'll never escape them.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: The shadows whispered among themselves and laid trap after trap to stop the puppet...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: The black-cloaked shadows didn't want to let the puppet make it any further. They did everything they could to try to get him to turn around.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Because if the puppet made it through the desert, hope would start to spread their way, and they would disappear.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: But the puppet didn't know that. His goal never once changed.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: The puppet made it past their traps and foiled their plans. All the tricks they had up their sleeves had failed. They were furious, and they decided they weren't going to hide anymore. They were going to duke it out with the puppet and fight him to the death.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: When he saw the shadows rushing toward him, the puppet took out a long spear made of a needle and some threads. Then, he—

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Theresa, why did they become the echoes of despair and sadness?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Well, about that...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Did they catch Oripathy? And the pain kept them up at night?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Then, maybe the puppet could cure them? Just like what you and Dr. Kal'tsit want to do.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Cure them?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: If the puppet cured them and turned them into... hm... happy and peaceful shadows, then everybody could go to the Plains of Hope together, right?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Were they born baddies who liked to scare people?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: No, dear, of course not.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: The puppet found out that... they all had wounds on their bodies. It was the wounds that turned them into who they were.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Couldn't he fix them up with his needle and thread? Just like what you always do!

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Maybe... Perhaps it's worth a try.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: (Yawns)

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Sleepy?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: N-No, I'm not! Did he do it?!

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: The puppet tried over and over. The stitches were thick and ugly. The black-cloaked shadows were livid.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Wh-What happened next...?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Maybe... peace and happiness don't really come so easily, but in the end, they decided to let the puppet go.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: The black-cloaked shadows watched the puppet walk into the distance. They decided they'd let the puppet give it a shot, but... a big river stood before him.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: He didn't even know how wide it was. All he knew was that he couldn't see the other side of the river.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: He knew that the Plains of Hope were on the other side, but there weren't any boats nearby. There wasn't even a decently sized frond.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: 'What do I do now?' The puppet thought to himself, and he decided to see if he could swim across.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: But... he's a... cloth puppet...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Right, he was made of cloth. If he got wet, he would only get heavier and heavier until he sank to the bottom of the river.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: But if he stopped here, his journey would have been for nothing.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: He leapt into the water and found that the river was cold and salty, like tears.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Apparently... a lot of people across the lands wanted to go to those plains, but not one of them succeeded.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: It was their tears that formed this river. The puppet finally understood just how many people shed tears over this.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Zzz...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: The puppet swam and swam. He felt his body slowly soaking up the tears.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Did the other side of the river really exist? Perhaps the shadows were right. It was called the 'Plains of Hope' because no one could truly make it there.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: People speak different languages, and their hearts are not connected.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Home. Home.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: But a river meant that there must also be a source to return to.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Sleep soundly, Amiya.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Good night.

a.text: Amiya has no idea how she got back to her room. That night, she slept very soundly.
Did the puppet make it across the shore? What happened in the end?
A ravine suddenly appeared. Just like that, the two sides have lost contact.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Ah! Doctor, when did you get back?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Is everyone waiting for me? I'm sorry. I'll just need a minute...

options: You did well during the battle.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Yeah!

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: It's okay, Doctor. I'm all ready.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Let's head over there together.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: We're about ready for departure. Every one of us has to leave Brentwood. Good thing these bones are large enough for us all to fit.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: The Military Commission must already have caught wind that we've taken control of the town and the Lifebone. It goes without saying that the skeleton is of tremendous importance.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Their counter-offensive might already be on the way. Perhaps the Sarkaz are watching our every move as we speak.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Ever since their rapid tactical unit, the Witchling, took to the skies... it's always felt like somebody's been watching us in the mist. It's unnerving.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: The battle will only get more dangerous from here on out.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: We all know that. The Exemplars will not give up their counter-offensive on Londinium. We have no other choice.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Victoria's people have endured this long enough already.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Good thing we seized the skeleton. Under ideal conditions, it will serve as a temporary stronghold. The wounded and civilians will also get to settle down a little.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Besides, if what Hoederer said is true, it can teleport anywhere, although it might make the users nauseous.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: This is indeed some much appreciated help, but something is bothering me...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Why wouldn't the Military Commission defend such an important transport to the death?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Perhaps they gave up because of the pressure of the battlefield, or perhaps Duq'arael... the Sanguinarch underestimated his enemies...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: But it's more likely that their plan in Londinium has already reached a stage where... they can't afford to worry about anything happening outside.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: The Sanguinarch still completed his final ritual. That may be exactly why they turned their gaze not to the Lifebone, but somewhere else.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Hoederer has finished negotiating with the consciousness left in the skeleton. It will... yes... 'listen to our proposal.' With its help, we will be able to return to the battlefield at any moment.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Most importantly, it gave us an opportunity to get close to the airship and the Shard.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: If we make use of this trump card well... Just maybe, we'll be able to mount an airborne assault on Central Londinium.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Take out their headquarters directly. Good. I like that.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: The area around the Shard is heavily guarded, and my guess is that the Military Commission's airship won't let us hover over their heads without a fight.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: All we can do is find an opening for our strike team to enter, and as soon as they've made it in, we'll have the Lifebone depart.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: That means the strike team can't retreat.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: But at the same time, we still have to get to the bottom of what's been bothering Amiya: What exactly are the Sarkaz planning?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: And how to foil their little tricks.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: We won't be able to take the Shard with this little time by ourselves, but... we still have friends inside that massive city. We need to get in touch with them.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: According to our intelligence, there likely aren't many combatants stationed inside the Shard.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Based on my experience fighting their commander, if Theresis... Amiya, what would you say our chances are?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: No, we should avoid a direct confrontation with him at all costs. No one is strong enough to singlehandedly defeat Theresis.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Besides, our greatest threat right now is not a single powerful Sarkaz hero. Rather, it is their ambition to see their plans come to fruition.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: We will only be able to end this war quickly by stopping it from happening.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: A few squads on their own can't end a war. We still need the Victorian military.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: It's true that the Duke of Windermere perishing on the front lines is beyond what any of us might have...

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Oh.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Forgive me... Lady Delphine.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Standing beside you now is an intelligence officer in the service of Duke Windermere, not her daughter.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Pay me no mind.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: The Duke of Windermere's untimely passing has disrupted the fragile balance on the outskirts of Londinium. They are on the brink of war.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Heh, until a few weeks ago, I was still under the impression that if the dukes were to put their minds to it and attack Londinium together, a Sarkaz defeat would have been all but assured.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: This will be a decisive battle, one far worse than what any of the bigwigs have been anticipating.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I'd like to say they wished this upon themselves, but it's the frontline soldiers and innocent citizens who are suffering right now.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: So, when the time comes... who's going to win? Us, the Exemplars, or the dukes?

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Uh, sorry, I guess I shouldn't be asking that before an operation?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: It's fine. I know what it is you're worried about.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: But there's no need to worry. A great many people stood up, raised their heads, and woke from their dreams because of this calamity, whether willingly or forced.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: You are far from the only ones.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: We need to focus on the problem at hand: How to break through the battlefield for our Londinium counter-offensive, as well as how to stop the Shard's strikes.

options: The next step in the Sarkaz plan most likely has to do with Originium.
It's very likely that they will apply ancient Sarkaz research on Originium.
We don't have time. We need to decide on a route for our advance.
Taking the battlefield head-on is our one and only choice.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: We received a transmission indicating we have several Rhodes Island support teams on the way.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: There are many things we will only be able to accomplish here as Rhodes Island.

options: I will see our strategy executed flawlessly.
And put this crisis behind us.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: It seems none of us have any objections. That being the case...
Everyone turns to Amiya.
Suddenly, you feel a hint of relief, gratification, excitement, and pride.
After all, you are standing right beside her.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: This war has come to a head, and Theresis intends to use some more decisive and forceful means to tear Victoria to shreds.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: This has nothing to do with whether the Sarkaz truly have a right to revenge. It has nothing to do with whether the nobles may bear this heavy burden for Victoria.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: If we solve all our problems by destroying our enemies, then this land, plagued by war from the beginning, has no hope.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: The Confessarii and Theresis are there, at the heart of Londinium, toppling this empire standing on shaky ground.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I will go to them. And I will stop them.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: For that future, and for the future of all.

spans.text: future, and for the future of all.

steps.name: W
steps.text: Isn't a big gap like this a waste?

steps.name: W
steps.text: I got some real juicy explosives from Closure, enough to pack every corner of this place full.

steps.name: W
steps.text: Hah, and they're still cooking up stupid ideas like mounting an attack on Londinium. This is the Military Commission we're talking about. Who knows what tricks Theresis's got up his sleeve?

spans.text: Hah, and they're still cooking up stupid ideas like mounting an attack on Londinium. This is the
we're talking about. Who knows what tricks Theresis's got up his sleeve?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: So?

steps.name: W
steps.text: Bomb the place, straight up.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Heh, why do you think the Military Commission went through all that trouble to hide this skeleton, instead of treating it as a second airship?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: This thing is fragile. It's only thanks to the witchcraft device that we can communicate with the Feranmut's lingering breath of life. An attack, no matter how weak, could spell the end of it.

steps.name: W
steps.text: You think I'm talking about dropping bombs out of it? I'm saying let's make it the bomb.

spans.text: You think I'm talking about dropping bombs out of it? I'm saying let's make

steps.name: W
steps.text: A bomb that can fly just about anywhere it wants, that can fly right into Theresis's face at any moment. The perfect bomb.

steps.name: W
steps.text: What? You're still thinking about letting it take us back to Kazdel? If we don't deal with Theresis, we aren't going anywhere.

steps.name: W
steps.text: Let's take the simplest path to solving our problems here.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: *sigh*.

steps.name: W
steps.text: Got something to share with the class?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Nothing at all, but I didn't expect to see you so tense.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Should I teach you a few deep breathing techniques?

steps.name: W
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Whatever, W. Get in the right frame of mind for this operation. Otherwise, no amount of explosives is going to fix what's going on in your head.

steps.name: W
steps.text: That just means we're gonna need even more bombs.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: If you say so.

steps.name: W
steps.text: Phew...

steps.name: W
steps.text: Ines.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: What?

steps.name: W
steps.text: Remember when we ran into that Lich the other day...? Never mind. Forget it—

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: You're wondering whether the Theresa out there's real or not again, aren't you?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Hmph, enough of that already. I'm not the one you need to convince.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: I wasn't the one who called her a fake first either.

steps.name: W
steps.text: Ugh... Did I ever tell you your Arts are disgusting?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: I didn't need to read your shadow. You've been pretty anxious for a while now.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: What will you do, if you run into her again?

steps.name: W
steps.text: I told you. It's a fake. I'm gonna kill it and be done with this.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: And what if it's not?

steps.name: W
steps.text: Then I'll rescue her and get to the bottom of everything.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: That's Theresa.

steps.name: W
steps.text: I know.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: I think you don't. You haven't figured out how to treat Theresa, how to handle an... enemy leader.

spans.text: I think you don't. You haven't figured out how to treat Theresa, how to handle an...

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: That's a taboo, and you know it far better than I do.

steps.name: W
steps.text: *Sarkaz expletive*, Ines. You know what pisses me off the most?

steps.name: W
steps.text: I remember a lot of stuff. I remember the crystal on the head of the old fart who taught me how to make explosives. I remember the prices on your heads...

steps.name: W
steps.text: I remember how Her Highness wrestled with that door, and how Kal'tsit once got her hair caught in the same door.

steps.name: W
steps.text: I remember all these things that don't fucking matter!

steps.name: W
steps.text: ...But I don't remember—

steps.name: W
steps.text: I can't for the life of me remember when the last time I saw her was, or even... what we talked about.

steps.name: W
steps.text: Yeah, yeah, I barely ever had a normal conversation with her.

steps.name: W
steps.text: There were so many of us on the ship. I was small potatoes, and she was Babel's chairman. It was probably a joke, some silly complaint or nagging—

steps.name: W
steps.text: But it definitely wasn't... a goodbye.

steps.name: W
steps.text: This time, I'll make up for that and say it. Then, I won't forget.

steps.name: W
steps.text: Anyways... I've gotta get my mercs checking over their equipment. This is gonna be one hell of a job.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Whatever you say.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: But if your legs give out on you and you need somebody to give you a good kick in the ass, you know who to call.

steps.name: W
steps.text: Yeah.

steps.name: W
steps.text: This nightmare has gone on long enough. We should be looking straight ahead.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: All preparations are complete. The airship is ready to take flight.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: It will all be over soon.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Come, walk with me one last time, Theresis.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Very well...

The Military Commission of Kazdel has secretly constructed airship docks just like this one in the support layers of several sectors throughout Londinium. This is the largest among them, and it is where the airship was born.
The ship is seen as a terrifying weapon of war, a herald of destruction, and a flying fortress.
But very few are aware of the original intent behind the airship's construction. It is to uncover a buried secret...
And, beyond that, it is to break free of an eternal shackle.
The brother and sister are walking in the great ship dock, down a long passageway, where every Sarkaz they pass stops and greets the two of them.
When was the last time they had a nice walk like this together? Thinking about it, compared to the amount of time they have spent together, the days that have passed is nothing.
But they were also long enough.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: What's on your mind, Theresa?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I suddenly remembered that when Kazdel was rebuilt into a nomadic city, we stood next to each other on the city walls, shoulder-to-shoulder, just like this.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: It was supposed to be a happy day, but then it rained.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Some said it was a bad omen, but I still remember how the Soul Furnace's flames looked all the brighter in the rain.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: And there's more. I'm suddenly remembering so, so much... It's been too long.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: It has been too long indeed.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: From Kazdel to Kazdel... our goal lies right before us. There is but one last step in our plan.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Those who walk after us will find a great city standing tall upon this land, and we Sarkaz will do as we wish, seizing control of our own fate.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: I need you.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Yes... I know.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: The warriors who once firmly believed in your path, the girl who is called the King of Sarkaz... They've all come before you now.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Of course they came. I've always believed they would.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Have you decided how you will confront them?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I've never once been confused, but... I had hoped this day would take longer to arrive. Now that it's come to this, I actually feel...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I underestimated those I should have had faith in.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Theresis, I'm delighted.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I'm delighted that even after we made this decision, they are still willing to stand up against us.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: They are decisive and strong, and they are growing at an unimaginable pace. Perhaps they will make their way to you in the end.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: They may be much stronger now than the woman I was... the one who couldn't accomplish anything.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: I'm looking forward to it.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Then... It's time for me to leave, too.
Theresa steps onto the airship's gangway, while Theresis remains where he stands, quietly watching her.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Theresa.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: This time, we should bid each other a proper farewell.
Theresa reaches her hand out and smooths out the creases on Theresis's cloak.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: ...(Ancient Sarkaz language) Goodbye.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: (Ancient Sarkaz language) Goodbye.
The silence lasts until the steel door closes and its thick shadow shrouds the two of them.
They say nothing more.
The pulsing of the myriad souls is ceaseless. Theresa lightly closes her eyes to bear with its surge.
The endless murmurs are like the tide. It exhausts, it drags those within it ever downward, and it suffocates.
Perhaps within it once existed brief moments of happiness or the occasional delight... but there is simply too much pain... so much that the pain permeates every word and sentence.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: O myriad souls... Even though I have almost completely exhausted myself, I still cannot see the other side.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Shattered hearts abound on these lands.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: And so, even if I have only grief at my disposal... even if my body was wrought of tears...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Be my oar, and be my ark.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Let tears carry tears, and let suffering lift up suffering.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: It's time that we... set sail.
Logos is examining the bone whistle in his hands. He knows every pattern carved into it and every wear and tear on its surface.
He remembers receiving this from his mother when he was still a small child. Its sound was not nearly as sonorous and vivid as it is now.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: So this is a Banshee's bone whistle. It's my first time seeing the real thing.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Banshees are a rare sight among mercenaries to begin with, much less one with a bone whistle.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: That said, I've heard plenty of stories about bone whistle—

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: It's a symbol of terror. Its sound foretells death's pursuit.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: The Banshees portend death, and willingly serve as the embodiment of death and danger.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: But I rarely ever saw you use the whistle, not at Babel all those years ago or at Rhodes Island now.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: The Vampire... accused you of rejecting the power of your bloodline.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: It already sounded. It need not sound again.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: Metaphors about death itself are a dime a dozen, but what comes after death?

spans.text: Metaphors about death itself are a dime a dozen, but what comes

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: True, the Banshees portend death, but nothing more.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: If death wasn't the end of all beings and there was more than nothingness after the toll of the death knell, then this foretelling would have been meaningless.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: That's why we set down the bone whistles for bone pens.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: New meaning is born from the pens' tips, while the past... is only recorded by the same tips.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: This is why we stand together now, Hoederer.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Is that right?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Yes, toward the other side of death. Rebirth.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: It matters not what Theresis intends to accomplish. This war will not and cannot be allowed to develop into a raging fire that destroys the Sarkaz, as history has seen countless times before.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Having burned for so long, this hatred cannot be easily extinguished, but we can stop it from engulfing all souls upon these lands.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: That includes each and every race there is.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Dr. {@nickname}, hold on tight.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: The final battle... is able to begin.
The Feranmut's skeleton wriggles its body and once again dives straight into history.
The fragments of time are like bubbles in a muddled stream. After they break up, the remains are still vague and indistinct.
Amiya feels the rippling spacetime rushing past her. You look at her and see her eyelashes twitching. What exactly does she see?
Perhaps nothing more than reflections passing by, or fleeting hallucinations.
The distance between memories and history is always much longer than we expect.
Countless sceneries, both ancient and modern, sweep by under the Feranmut's frame.
Those who find themselves within are astonished by this advancement or regression of times, the disasters that unfold before them, and the happiness in their hands...
But when looking upon them from high above, perhaps these sights have never actually changed.
Then, the illusion grows much stranger and more twisted.
A seed is rapaciously absorbing nutrients. It writhes, whimpers, trying to tear away all fabricated representation.
This creation, far beyond human comprehension, waits silently. The slightest movement is enough to rend the continent and allow the crystals to proliferate.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: No, this isn't right.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: This isn't the Feranmut's power!

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: The sky... The entire sky is burning red!

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: The Lifebone is out of control. It's been pulled off its original course!

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Are we under attack?

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Guard the entrances to all cabins! Watch for attacking aircraft!

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: We're preparing anti-boarding measures. All non-combatants, retreat to your shelters!

steps.name: W
steps.text: Mercs, fan out! Don't let any drooling morons onto the ship!

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Any damage reports?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I'm checking, but—What's going on? This makes no sense!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: The sensors I set up are all reading normal. The skeleton's not damaged at all!

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I just got word from the observation post. They've spotted no enemies!

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: We're losing altitude! I can't control it!

steps.name: W
steps.text: What the *Sarkaz expletive* is happening?

steps.name: W
steps.text: Isn't this skeleton your best friend, Hoederer? Get it to chill out!

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Hoederer, can you adjust the course at all? We mustn't land in the center of the battlefield!

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: I'm trying!

steps.name: W
steps.text: Buckle up, everybody. I don't want anyone getting flung out through the gaps in the bones!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I've sent out all my drones to try to pull the Feranmut's bones back and reduce the impact of the crash!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Don't get your hopes up, though!

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Our descent isn't slowing. Going by the current speed...

options: We'll hit the ground very soon.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: 'The meaning of language shall grant us wings.'

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: 'I command these words to lift this weight.'

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: It's working—

steps.name: W
steps.text: Keep chanting your incantations, Banshee. Hoederer, keep steering us north!

steps.name: W
steps.text: There's a valley there. We should fit right in!

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: I'm on it, but my link with the Feranmut is fading. I can't control it much longer!

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Mon3tr.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: (Excited howling)

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Protect the Doctor. Prepare for impact.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: (Joyful howling)

options: Its claws are digging into me!

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Calm down, Doctor. You'll be fine.

steps.name: W
steps.text: Amiya, how are things going over—

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: All the wounded and civilians have been relocated. Feist and Rockrock are working on getting the transport secured.

steps.name: W
steps.text: Got it. Ines, my mercs have anything to say?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: They're all here with me, working on getting some witchcraft going.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: We'll need a little more time. We should be able to withstand half of the impact's force.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Tell Hoederer these bones won't shatter here.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: The valley's in sight. Our angle's not quite there yet. We need to turn left by another twenty degrees!

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Last chance for adjustments!

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Twenty degrees, I'm certain of it!

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: All hands, brace for impact!

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: The rest comes down to luck!

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Ten seconds to impact!

steps.name: W
steps.text: Five, four, three—

steps.name: W
steps.text: Two!

steps.name: W
steps.text: One!
